BURSEVI:v10p253/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p253/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p253/r1.claim: Marʿaha means pasture; water and grazing are attributed to the earth because they emerge from it, and this clause explains or completes the earth’s preparation for habitation.
BURSEVI:v10p253/r1.anchor: أي رعيها بالكسر بمعنى الكلأ وهو في الأصل موضع الرعي بالفتح

BIQAI-FULL:v8p308#s079/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p308#s079/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p308#s079/r1.claim: The surah’s purpose is to establish resurrection and the gathering, displaying humanity’s final fate after the preceding surahs’ full exposition; its oaths show the matter has reached its decisive climax.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p318/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p318/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p318/r1.claim: Night and day recur as daily demonstrations of resurrection, since restoring life is no harder than creating humanity from nothing.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p318/r1.anchor: ولما كان كل من ذلك يدل على القدرة على البعث لأنه إيجاد ما هو أشد من خلق الآدمي من عدم

BIQAI-FULL:v8p318/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p318/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p318/r4.claim: Earth’s water comes from within it, as its possessive attribution indicates; its pasture includes what is grazed, its place, and its season.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p318/r4.anchor: بتفجير العيون , وإضافته إليها دليل على أنه فيها

DURR-FULL:v8p412/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p412/r2.speaker: ابن جريج
DURR-FULL:v8p412/r2.claim: Ibn Jurayj glosses the water as rivers made to flow and pasture as all the plants and other growth God created.

JISHUMI:v10p7271#2/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7271#2/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7271#2/r10.claim: Marʿā is vegetation fit for grazing, named from the livestock grazing on and eating it.
JISHUMI:v10p7271#2/r10.anchor: والمرعى: النبات الذي يصلح لرعي الماشية، وهي ترعاه بأن تأكله

TABATABAI:79:27-34/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:79:27-34/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:79:27-34/r9.claim: Bringing out Earth's water means releasing springs and rivers; its pasture is all vegetation eaten by humans and animals, not only animal fodder.
TABATABAI:79:27-34/r9.anchor: فالظاهر أن المراد بالمرعى مطلق النبات الذي يتغذى به الحيوان والانسان

TABRISI:79:27-46#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:79:27-46#2/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:79:27-46#2/r6.claim: The water God brought out includes rivers, seas, and springs; the pasture includes food for people and animals.
TABRISI:79:27-46#2/r6.anchor: المعنى فجر الأنهار والبحار والعيون عن ابن عباس

TABRISI:79:27-46#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:79:27-46#2/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:79:27-46#2/r7.claim: Water sustains animals, trees, fruit, grain, and springs, while pasture supplies livestock; these together cover earthly benefits and provisions.
TABRISI:79:27-46#2/r7.anchor: وبها يحصل جميع الأرزاق والنبات التي تصلح للمواشي فهي ترعاه بأن تأكله في موضعه

SAMIN-DURR:79:31/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:79:31/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:79:31/r1.claim: أخرج may be an explanatory clause or a circumstantial clause.
SAMIN-DURR:79:31/r1.anchor: أخرج }: فيه وجهان، أحدهما: أن يكون تفسيرا. والثاني: أن يكون حالا.

SAMIN-DURR:79:31/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:79:31/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:79:31/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī explains why the verb lacks conjunction: دحاها means spread and prepared the earth for habitation, then أخرج details provisions needed for dwelling and settlement.
SAMIN-DURR:79:31/r2.anchor: قال الزمخشري: " فإن قلت: فهلا أدخل حرف العطف على " أخرج ". قلت: فيه وجهان

SAMIN-DURR:79:31/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:79:31/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:79:31/r3.claim: The circumstantial analysis supplies an implicit قد, as in 4:90; al-Samīn says this is the majority view, opposed by the Kufans and al-Akhfash.
SAMIN-DURR:79:31/r3.anchor: قلت: إضمار " قد " هو قول الجمهور، وخالف الكوفيون والأخفش.

SAMIN-DURR:79:33/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:79:33/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:79:33/r2.claim: Al-marʿā can be a place noun, time noun, or verbal noun; here it is a verbal noun with passive-object sense, used metaphorically of people.
SAMIN-DURR:79:33/r2.anchor: والمرعى في الأصل: مكان أو زمان أو مصدر، وهو هنا مصدر بمعنى المفعول، وهو في حق الآدميين استعارة.

ASAD-NOTES:79:27#n14/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:79:27#n14/r1.speaker: Razi
ASAD-NOTES:79:27#n14/r1.claim: Razi explains pasture metonymically as all herbal produce suitable for human or animal consumption.
ASAD-NOTES:79:27#n14/r1.anchor: The term "pasture" (mar'a) connotes here, metonymically, all herbal produce suitable for consumption by man or animal (Razi).

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1077/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1077/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1077/r2.claim: After the separation, bringing forth the earth's water and pasture and setting its mountains are later developmental stages, not creation itself.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1077/r2.anchor: الأرض أخرج ماءها ومرعاها والجبال أرساها هذه أطوار وهي أمور أخرى

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1077/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1077/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1077/r3.claim: دحاها means spread or expanded the earth, not created it; this describes a later form after the heavens and earth were created together.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1077/r3.anchor: لم يقل خلقها وإنما دحاها أي بسطها كانت مع السماء ثم فتقها وبسطها

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1077/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1077/r4.speaker: من يقول أن الدحي هي بيضة النعام
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1077/r4.claim: Some interpret the earth's dahw as making it spherical, comparing the shape to an ostrich egg.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1077/r4.anchor: أو جعلها كرة على رأي من يقول أن الدحي هي بيضة النعام

ALUSI-FULL:v30p34/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p34/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p34/r1.claim: God brought out the earth's water by opening springs and causing rivers to flow.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p34/r1.anchor: بأن فجر منها عيونا وأجرى أنهارا ومرعاها يقع

ALUSI-FULL:v30p34/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p34/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p34/r2.claim: Marʿā can mean pasture or fodder, grazing as a verbal noun, or a place or time; although some make place its original sense, fodder best fits this context.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p34/r2.anchor: يقع على الرعي بالكسر وهو الكلأ والرعي بالفتح وهو المصدر وكذا على الموضع والزمان

ALUSI-FULL:v30p34/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p34/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p34/r3.claim: Some restrict pasture to what animals eat and extend it to human food by metonymy; al-Tibi allows an explicit metaphor, addressing resurrection-deniers as people yoked with beasts in worldly enjoyment and heedlessness of the afterlife.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p34/r3.anchor: وقال الطيبي يجوز أن يكون استعارة مصرحة لأن الكلام مع منكري الحشر

ALUSI-FULL:v30p34/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p34/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p34/r4.claim: The phrase explains and completes the earth's spreading: settlement requires provision for livelihood, including food and drink; syntactically it can also be a circumstantial clause with an implicit qad, either way without a conjunction.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p34/r4.anchor: بيان وتفسير لدحاها وتكملة له فإن السكنى لا تتأتى بمجرد البسط

BAYDAWI-FULL:79:27-31/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:79:27-31/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:79:27-31/r8.claim: He brought its water out by making springs gush forth.

BAYDAWI-FULL:79:27-31/r9.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:79:27-31/r9.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:79:27-31/r9.claim: Marʿāhā means grazing or pasture, though originally it denotes the place where animals graze.
BAYDAWI-FULL:79:27-31/r9.anchor: ورعيها وهو في الأصل لموضع الرعي

BAYDAWI-FULL:79:27-31/r10.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:79:27-31/r10.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:79:27-31/r10.claim: The sentence is separated from its conjunction because it is circumstantial with an implicit qad, or because it explains the earth's spreading.
BAYDAWI-FULL:79:27-31/r10.anchor: وتجريد الجملة عن العاطف لأنها حال بإضمار قد أو بيان للدحو

BINTSHATI:v1p151/r8.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p151/r8.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p151/r8.claim: Marʿā is derived from grazing and its form can be a verbal noun or a noun of time or place; the likeliest sense here is what is grazed, as in al-Aʿla.
BINTSHATI:v1p151/r8.anchor: والصيغة تحتمل أن تكون للمصدر وللزمان والمكان، لكن الأرجح أن المراد به هنا ما يرعى

BINTSHATI:v1p152/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p152/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p152/r1.claim: Grazing primarily concerns camels and livestock; applying it metaphorically to people is familiar in Arabic, as in shepherd and flock.
BINTSHATI:v1p152/r1.anchor: والأصل في الرعى أن يكون للإبل والأنعام، وقد جاء بهذا المعنى في آية طه 54

BINTSHATI:v1p152/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p152/r2.speaker: أبو حيان
BINTSHATI:v1p152/r2.claim: Abu Hayyan says water precedes pasture because it causes the pasture to grow.
BINTSHATI:v1p152/r2.anchor: وفي تقديم الماء على المرعى، بآية النازعات، يقول أبو حيان: إن الماء سبب المرعى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p86/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p86/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p86/r7.claim: “He brought out its water and pasture” is a بدل اشتمال construction from “spread it,” because the two verbs have different meanings and the earth’s useful contents complete its spread.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p86/r7.anchor: وجملة { أخرج منها ماءها ومرعاها } بدل اشتمال من جملة { دحاها }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p86/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p86/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p86/r8.claim: Al-marʿā derives from raʿā; here it is a verbal noun used for its object, meaning what is grazed.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p86/r8.anchor: والمرعى : مفعل من رعى يرعى ، وهو هنا مصدر ميمي أطلق على المفعول كالخلق بمعنى المخلوق

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p87/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p87/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p87/r1.claim: Grazing literally means livestock consuming pasture, grass, and fresh fodder.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p87/r1.anchor: والرعي : حقيقته تناول الماشية الكلأ والحشيش والقصيل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p87/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p87/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p87/r2.claim: Mentioning pasture suffices for fruits and grain: if God cares for animals, humans deserve care even more; 79:33 signals this ellipsis.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p87/r2.anchor: فالاقتصار على المرعى اكتفاء عن ذكر ما تخرجه الأرض من الثمار والحبوب لأن ذكر المرعى يدل على لطف الله بالعجماوات

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p87/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p87/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p87/r3.claim: Water and pasture stand for all the earth’s provisions for people and animals, including cooking fuel such as wood and salt from water on earth.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p87/r3.anchor: وقد دل بذكر الماء والمرعى على جميع ما تخرجه الأرض قوتا للناس وللحيوان حتى ما تعالج به الأطعمة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p23/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p23/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p23/r1.claim: God caused springs to gush from the earth, and its pasture is what people and animals eat.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p23/r1.anchor: أي فجر العيون منها ومرعاها وهو ما يأكله الناس والأنعام

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p316#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p316#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس وابن جرير
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p316#2/r2.claim: Spreading earth means bringing its potential contents into actuality; it was created before the sky but spread after it. Ibn al-Jarir chooses this reading.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p316#2/r2.anchor: أن الأرض خلقت قبل السماء، ولكن إنما دحيت بعد خلق السماء، بمعنى أنه أخرج ما كان فيها بالقوة إلى الفعل.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p316#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p316#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p316#2/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas says spreading the earth brought out water and pasture, split rivers, and placed mountains, sands, roads, and hills.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p316#2/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس: {دحاها} ودحيها أن أخرج منها الماء والمرعى

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p697#2/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p697#2/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p697#2/r7.claim: Its water means springs that gush forth.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p697#2/r7.anchor: { ماءها } عيونها المتفجرة بالماء { ومرعاها } ورعيها

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p697#2/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p697#2/r8.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p697#2/r8.claim: Marʿāhā means its grazing or pasture, originally the place where grazing occurs.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p697#2/r8.anchor: { ومرعاها } ورعيها ، وهو في الأصل موضع الرعى

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p697#2/r10.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p697#2/r10.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p697#2/r10.claim: Two explanations account for the lack of a conjunction before ‘He brought forth’: it explains what spreading earth entails, or it is a circumstantial clause with an implied qad.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p697#2/r10.anchor: أحدهما : أن يكون معنى { دحاها } بسطها ومهدها للسكنى ، ثم فسر التمهيد بما لا بد منه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p697#2/r11.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p697#2/r11.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p697#2/r11.claim: Pasture includes what people and animals eat; grazing is metaphorically used for people as in ‘roam and play,’ and one reading uses nartaʿu.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p697#2/r11.anchor: وأراد بمرعاها : ما يأكل الناس والأنعام . واستعير الرعي للإنسان كما استعير الرتع في قوله : { نخوض ونلعب }

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p697#2/r12.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p697#2/r12.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p697#2/r12.claim: Mentioning water and pasture signals all earthly benefits and enjoyments, even salt, since salt comes from water.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p697#2/r12.anchor: دل الله سبحانه بذكر الماء والمرعى على عامة ما يرتفق به ويتمتع مما يخرج من الأرض حتى الملح

MUQATIL:79:27-33/r9.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:79:27-33/r9.speaker: author
MUQATIL:79:27-33/r9.claim: The earth's water means its seas, and its pasture its plants, since both come from the earth.
MUQATIL:79:27-33/r9.anchor: يقول: بحورها ونباتها لأن النبات والماء يكونان من الأرض

NASAFI-FULL:v4p315#9/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p315#9/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p315#9/r1.claim: He brought out the earth's water by causing springs to gush, and its pasture means its forage.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p315#9/r1.anchor: ﴿ أخرج منها ماءها ﴾ بتفجير العيون ﴿ ومرعاها ﴾ كلأها

NASAFI-FULL:v4p315#9/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p315#9/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p315#9/r2.claim: Nasafi notes that no coordinating conjunction precedes akhraja.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p315#9/r2.anchor: ولذا لم يدخل العاطف على أخرج

NASAFI-FULL:v4p315#9/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p315#9/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p315#9/r3.claim: Alternatively, akhraja is a circumstantial clause with an implicit qad.

QURTUBI-FULL:79:31-33/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:79:31-33/r13.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:79:31-33/r13.claim: The water brought out from earth means its gushing springs; its pasture means plants grazed by animals.

QURTUBI-FULL:79:31-33/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:79:31-33/r14.speaker: القتبي
QURTUBI-FULL:79:31-33/r14.claim: Al-Qutaybi says these two items stand for all earthly provision: grasses, trees, grain, dates, chaff, firewood, clothes, fire, and salt.
QURTUBI-FULL:79:31-33/r14.anchor: وقال القتبي: دل بشيئين على جميع ما أخرجه من الأرض قوتا ومتاعا للأنام من العشب والشجر والحب والتمر

QURTUBI-FULL:79:31-33/r17.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:79:31-33/r17.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:79:31-33/r17.claim: The lack of a conjunction before akhraja is explained by an implicit qad making it circumstantial, like 4:90.
QURTUBI-FULL:79:31-33/r17.anchor: ويقال: هلا أدخل حرف العطف على «أخرج» فيقال: إنه حال بإضمار قد

RAZI-FULL:v31p44/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p44/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p44/r8.claim: Another reading makes daḥāhā mean preparing earth to produce provisions, an aptitude that comes only after heaven exists, like a father with earth as mother.
RAZI-FULL:v31p44/r8.anchor: المراد أنه بسطها بسطا مهيأ لنبات الأقوات

RAZI-FULL:v31p45#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p45#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p45#2/r1.claim: The water is earth’s erupting springs; pasture means grazing, originally the place where grazing occurs.
RAZI-FULL:v31p45#2/r1.anchor: ماؤها عيونها المتفجرة بالماء ومرعاها رعيها

RAZI-FULL:v31p45#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p45#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p45#2/r2.claim: “Earth” and “mountains” are accusative through omitted verbs explained by the later predicates; al-Ḥasan reads both nominative as subjects.
RAZI-FULL:v31p45#2/r2.anchor: ونصب الأرض والجبال بإضمار دحا وأرسى

RAZI-FULL:v31p45#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p45#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p45#2/r3.claim: The missing conjunction before “brought forth” can be explained by taking spreading as preparation for habitation, then specifying water, pasture, food, and mountains that stabilize the earth.

RAZI-FULL:v31p45#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p45#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p45#2/r4.claim: Alternatively, “He brought forth” is a circumstantial clause: earth was spread while its water and pasture were brought forth.

RAZI-FULL:v31p45#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p45#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p45#2/r5.claim: Pasture includes what people and animals eat, as in 16:10’s water and grazing plants and 80:25–32’s account of food and provision.
RAZI-FULL:v31p45#2/r5.anchor: أراد بمرعاها ما يأكل الناس والأنعام

RAZI-FULL:v31p45#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p45#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p45#2/r6.claim: The text metaphorically applies grazing to humans, as with “graze and play”; the reading nartaʿ in 12:12 derives from grazing.
RAZI-FULL:v31p45#2/r6.anchor: واستعير الرعي للإنسان كما استعير الرتع

RAZI-FULL:v31p45#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p45#2/r7.speaker: ابن قتيبة
RAZI-FULL:v31p45#2/r7.claim: Ibn Qutayba takes water and pasture to encompass earth’s provisions and comforts: plants, grains, fruit, wood, clothing, medicine, fire from trees, and salt from water; worldly pleasures stem from water and plants.
RAZI-FULL:v31p45#2/r7.anchor: ثم قال ابن قتيبة قال تعالى

RAZI-FULL:v31p45#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p45#2/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p45#2/r8.claim: Rāzī takes the later statement that these are provision for people and livestock as evidence that pasture means everything eaten by both.
RAZI-FULL:v31p45#2/r8.anchor: يدل على أنه تعالى أراد بالمرعى كل ما يأكله الناس والأنعام

STUDYQURAN:79:31/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:79:31/r1.speaker: some
STUDYQURAN:79:31/r1.claim: Some take the pastures as an allusion to all plant life.
STUDYQURAN:79:31/r1.anchor: Its pastures is interpreted by some as an allusion to all plant life

STUDYQURAN:79:31/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:79:31/r2.speaker: others
STUDYQURAN:79:31/r2.claim: Others understand the pastures as everything eaten by human beings and animals.
STUDYQURAN:79:31/r2.anchor: and by others as an allusion to everything eaten by human beings and animals.

TAB-FULL:v24p96/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p96/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p96/r1.claim: God caused rivers to flow from the earth and made its plants grow.

TAB-FULL:v24p96/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p96/r2.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v24p96/r2.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk explains the water as rivers God made flow and the pasture as the plants He created there.

THALABI:v10p128/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p128/r5.speaker: القتيبي
THALABI:v10p128/r5.claim: Al-Qutaybi says water and pasture summarize all earthly food and utility, including plants, grain, dates, chaff, wood, clothing, fire, and salt; fire comes from wood and salt from water.
THALABI:v10p128/r5.anchor: قال القتيبي: أنظر كيف دل بشيئين على جميع ما أخرجه من الأرض قوتا ومتاعا للأنعام من العشب والشجر والحب والتمر والعصف والحطب واللباس والنار والملح

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p197/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p197/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p197/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says God brought forth the seas, rivers, springs, and all water.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p197/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يريد فجر البحار والأنهار، والعيون، وجميع الماء (¬1).

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p197/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p197/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p197/r2.claim: Marʿā means what people and livestock eat.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p197/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p197/r3.speaker: عبد الله بن مسلم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p197/r3.claim: Abdullah ibn Muslim says water and pasture summarize all earthly provision and benefits: plants, crops, fruit, fuel, clothing, fire from wood, and salt from water.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p197/r3.anchor: قال عبد الله بن مسلم: انظر كيف دل بشيئين على جميع ما أخرجه من الأرض: قوتا ومتاعا للأنام

ELMALILI:79:27-33/r20.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:79:27-33/r20.speaker: author
ELMALILI:79:27-33/r20.claim: God brought forth Earth’s water by creating it, gushing its springs and flowing its rivers, and made its grasses, pastures, and cultivated growth appear.
ELMALILI:79:27-33/r20.anchor: suyunu yarattı, menbalarını fışkırttı, nehirlerini akıttı, otunu, otlağını mezrasını bitirdi.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:27/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:27/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:27/r1.claim: The vast, complex, ordered cosmos is evidence to resurrection deniers that its creator can raise people again; another verse says creating heaven and earth is greater than creating humanity.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:27/r1.anchor: böylesine geniş ve kompleks olan, düzenli ve uyumlu işleyen varlıklar dünyasını yaratan kudretin insanları da öldükten sonra tekrar diriltebileceğine işaret edilmiştir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:27/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:27/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:27/r4.claim: Making earth habitable and furnishing it with provisions for people and animals also demonstrates God's power to resurrect.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:27/r4.anchor: yeryüzünü üzerinde yaşanacak bir şekilde yaratıp gerek insanların gerekse hayvanların beslenmesi için her türlü nimetlerle donatması

BURHAN:v1p475#3/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p475#3/r1.speaker: الشيخ
BURHAN:v1p475#3/r1.claim: An unnamed shaykh ruled that one may not drink water in which Qur'anic writing was washed, on the ground that it meets internal impurity.
BURHAN:v1p475#3/r1.anchor: وأفتى الشيخ أيضا بالمنع من أن يشرب شيئا كتب من القرآن لأنه تلاقيه النجاسة الباطنة

BURHAN:v1p475#3/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p475#3/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p475#3/r2.claim: The author objects that impurity in its original location has no legal consequence.
BURHAN:v1p475#3/r2.anchor: وفيما قاله لأنها في معدنها لا حكم لها

BURHAN:v1p475#3/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p475#3/r3.speaker: العماد النيهى
BURHAN:v1p475#3/r3.claim: Al-ʿImād al-Nihy permits washing a written Qur'anic scrap and drinking its water, though he forbids swallowing the paper itself; the author saw this in Ibn al-Ṣalāḥ's hand.
BURHAN:v1p475#3/r3.anchor: العماد النيهى تلميذ البغوى فيما رأيته بخط ابن الصلاح قال لا يجوز ابتلاع رقعة فيها آية من القرآن فلو غسلها وشرب ماءها جاز

BURHAN:v1p475#3/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p475#3/r4.speaker: القاضى الحسين
BURHAN:v1p475#3/r4.claim: Al-Qāḍī al-Ḥusayn and al-Rāfiʿī permit eating foods on which some Qur'anic writing has been placed.
BURHAN:v1p475#3/r4.anchor: وجزم القاضى الحسين والرافعى بجواز أكل الأطعمة التى كتب عليها شىء من القرآن

BURHAN:v1p475#3/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p475#3/r5.speaker: البيهقى
BURHAN:v1p475#3/r5.claim: Al-Bayhaqī transmits from al-Sulamī that Manṣūr ibn ʿAmmār found a paper bearing the basmala, ate it out of reverence, and thereafter received wisdom in a dream.
BURHAN:v1p475#3/r5.anchor: وقال البيهقى أخبرنا أبو عبد الرحمن السلمى فى ذكر منصور بن عمار أنه أوتى الحكمة وقيل إن سبب ذلك

BURHAN:v3p225/r9.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p225/r9.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p225/r9.claim: The two terms water and pasture encompass the earth's provisions and uses, including plants, grain, dates, fuel, clothing, fire, and salt.
BURHAN:v3p225/r9.anchor: فدل بأمرين على ججميع ما أخرجه من الأرض

ITQAN:v3p147/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p147/r6.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p147/r6.claim: The two terms encompass all earthly provisions and benefits, including vegetation, crops, fruit, straw, wood, clothing, fire, and salt.
ITQAN:v3p147/r6.anchor: دل بهاتين الكلمتين على جميع ما أخرجه من الأرض قوتا ومتاعا للأنام من العشب والشجر

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p11/r7.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p11/r7.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p11/r7.claim: Mentioning water and pasture stands for all food and provisions brought from earth: grass, trees, grain, fruit, firewood, leaves, clothing, fire, and salt; fire comes from branches and salt from water.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p11/r7.anchor: كيف دل بشيئين على جميع ما أخرجه من الأرض قوتا ومتاعا للأنام
